clue.text: Wide but not a first-class highway

parts.note: something not first class is second class, graded B
a road is a highway

explanation.surface: A complaint that a wide highway has not been given top classification.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a B road is a secondary road, a grade below an A road, so 'not a first-class highway' doubles as the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad and wide are synonyms describing great width.

clue.text: Drunk iron in being artificially fostered!

indicators.note: the iron symbol is placed in the middle of the word for drunk

parts.note: bottled is British slang for drunk
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a baby reared with iron supplements in its feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottled' is everyday British slang for very drunk; FE goes inside it before the final D.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby raised on formula from a bottle rather than at the breast is nourished artificially.

clue.text: That's what you think

parts.note: usually a dismissive retort, here read literally as describing a personal view

explanation.definitionFit: A view or belief held by someone is what they think about a matter.

clue.text: What a fool to use drugs

definitions.meaning: a fool or idiot can be called this
to drug or administer narcotics, as with a racehorse

explanation.surface: Someone scorns the stupidity of taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a stupid person and also a verb meaning to drug or take narcotics.

clue.text: Officer finds ancient city motor vandalised where law sittings are held

parts.note: CO is short for Commanding Officer
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: something vandalised is wrecked and broken up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A police officer discovers that a car from an old town has been smashed up near the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motor' looks like part of the surface's car story, but 'vandalised' tells you to scramble its letters, placed after the officer and the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hears cases in this chamber during sessions of a court.

clue.text: Not in the majority

parts.note: reads as being in a minority group, but majority here means legal adulthood

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the age of majority, when one becomes a legal adult, is eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone younger than the age of adulthood is legally a minor.

clue.text: Chancy way to raise a little money

definitions.text: Chancy way to raise a little money

parts.words: Chancy way to raise a little money
parts.note: sounds like risky fundraising, but describes flipping a coin into the air to decide by chance

explanation.definitionFit: Flipping a coin into the air settles a choice by heads or tails.

clue.text: Went all round the world

parts.note: suggests a globetrotter, but describes a satellite circling the earth

explanation.definitionFit: A satellite circling a planet travels around it in a fixed path.

clue.text: Chief officer in chains

parts.note: suggests a captured leader, but refers to the ceremonial chain of office worn by a civic head

explanation.definitionFit: The civic head of a town wears a ceremonial chain of office on formal occasions.

clue.text: Journeyed perhaps but stumbled

definitions.meaning: went on a trip or outing
caught a foot and fell forward

explanation.surface: A traveller who made a journey but kept losing their footing.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on an excursion and catching one's foot are both senses of the same past-tense verb.

clue.text: Place of instruction for those who want to make progress

definitions.text: Place of instruction for those who want to make progress

parts.words: Place of instruction for those who want to make progress
parts.note: sounds like an academy for the ambitious, but progress here is literal movement along a road

explanation.definitionFit: Learner motorists take lessons from an instructor before their test.

clue.text: Naughty boys die if they do not do as they are told!

definitions.text: do not do as they are told

indicators.note: naughty means badly behaved, so these letters misbehave into a new order

explanation.surface: A parent's grim warning that badly behaved children will perish if they ignore instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' rearranges the seven letters of BOYS DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse to follow instructions or orders is to defy them.

clue.text: Put down a lid that was broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: Someone sets down a cracked lid.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed or set on a surface is the past tense of lay.

clue.text: Diana and Raymond shortly producing record that is dated

indicators.note: producing suggests making something new out of the pieces, so they are rearranged

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diana
Ray is the short form of Raymond

explanation.surface: Two people's names are combined to create a dated document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts both names to DI and RAY; 'producing' then rearranges those five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily journal keeps an entry under each date.

clue.text: One out of step, a leading entertainer

annotationWithheld.why: 'One out of step, a leading entertainer' (4) for STAR: 'a leading entertainer' defines it, but no parse of 'One out of step' gives STAR, and no source found the clue to explain it.
annotationWithheld.clue: One out of step, a leading entertainer

clue.text: Natural aptitude of blonde accepting pound

indicators.note: the word for blonde takes in the letter for pound, holding it inside

parts.note: fair hair is blonde
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A blonde's natural talent includes taking money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts L inside FAIR, after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural talent or gift for something is a knack.

clue.text: The changes in writing for some spirits

indicators.note: the rearranged article goes inside the abbreviation for writing

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

indicators.note: the letters of the word change their order

explanation.surface: Revisions made to a manuscript about some drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' scrambles the clue's opening word, and 'in' puts the result inside the manuscript abbreviation. Meths is British shorthand for methylated spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Methylated spirits are denatured alcohol, usually shortened in Britain to this word.

clue.text: The last thing an investor expects to receive

definitions.text: The last thing an investor expects to receive

parts.words: The last thing an investor expects to receive
parts.note: reads as something an investor never expects, but means the closing payout of a company's financial year

explanation.definitionFit: A company pays shareholders its closing payout for the year after the accounts are settled.

clue.text: Penny mentioned that it was liked better

parts.note: referred to means mentioned

explanation.surface: Penny remarked that she favoured something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name but gives the coin abbreviation P.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour one option over another is to choose it as better.

clue.text: What a demolition gang may do to be exceedingly funny

definitions.text: What a demolition gang may do
definitions.meaning: a wrecking crew topples a building
make an audience roar with laughter

explanation.surface: A demolition crew that is hilarious at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally toppling a building, and idiomatically making an audience roar with laughter.

clue.text: Charm the said second-class sorceress

indicators.note: the said means as spoken, so the letters are what the phrase sounds like

parts.note: a second-class sorceress is a B witch, B being the second grade

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be enchanted by a rather inferior witch.
explanation.walkthrough: B stands for second class; 'B witch' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant or captivate someone is to cast a spell over them.

clue.text: Social gathering does not start with anointing

indicators.note: the word for a social gathering loses its opening letter

parts.note: a function is a formal social event

explanation.surface: A party gets going without a religious blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: The ritual application of holy oil is a sacramental rite.

clue.text: See 19
Refuse to find Dead Sea in Antarctica

parts.note: the Ross Sea is a bay of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica

explanation.surface: An instruction to locate the Dead Sea at the South Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the noun (rubbish), not the verb. 'Dead Sea' tempts as one place, but splits into D and the Ross Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste matter or rubbish skimmed off molten metal, and so worthless stuff generally.

clue.text: Incomplete protection given by debris

indicators.note: the word for protection is left unfinished, losing its last letter

parts.note: a screen gives protection or shelter

explanation.surface: A shield that only partially covers someone from flying rubble.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose broken rock fragments collect on mountain slopes.

clue.text: Port that's a credit to the east

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit; that the letters also run on through 'a credit' is a coincidence, the parse being a charade
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A harbour that brings credit to the eastern lands.
explanation.walkthrough: Acre is a historic port city in northern Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre is an ancient harbour town on the coast of Israel, an example of the category.

clue.text: It is dry in the Kalahari Desert

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A remark that the African desert is parched.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched land with little rainfall is a synonym.

clue.text: Not a stiff way to walk!

explanation.surface: A light-hearted note on walking without rigidity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means floppy rather than rigid, and also a hobbling gait favouring one leg.

clue.text: Remarkably not a river in Spain lake

indicators.note: remarkably suggests an unusual form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: rio is the Spanish word for river

explanation.surface: Surprise that a Spanish lake is not a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkably' rearranges NOTA into ONTA. Lake Ontario is one of the North American Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is one of the five Great Lakes on the US-Canada border, an example of the category.

clue.text: The louder I snore, I become agitated

indicators.note: agitated letters are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A sleeper confesses that the more they snore, the more restless they get.
explanation.definitionFit: Making more racket or sound is a comparative synonym.

clue.text: She'd clued differently as arranged

indicators.note: the letters are set in a different order

explanation.surface: A setter wrote her clues another way, as agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges SHE'D CLUED, ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Planned or fixed for a particular time is a synonym of organised in advance.

clue.text: Had an intense desire quietly to dine out

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, meaning quietly

indicators.note: out suggests letters thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone longed to go out to eat in peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'dine out' but tells you to scramble DINE after the musical P.
explanation.definitionFit: Longing or yearning for something is to ache for it.
